text.brief: On March 17, 1959, the Dalai Lama slipped out of the Norbulingka palace in Lhasa in disguise and began a two-week flight to India.
text.record: Tibetans had risen against Party rule in Lhasa on March 10, and Party artillery shelled the city after the Dalai Lama left. Two CIA-trained Tibetans radioed news of his flight, and the agency trained Tibetan fighters at Camp Hale in Colorado from 1958 to 1964 ([CIA: Spy Sites, Camp Hale](https://www.cia.gov/stories/story/spy-sites-camp-hale/)). Washington wound the program down as it moved toward the Party in the late 1960s and early 1970s.
text.reading: The United States ran the borrowed knife on the Party's frontier and withdrew it when strategy changed, and the Tibetans who fought paid the cost. A patron who arms a resistance and then leaves teaches every later partner what the patronage is worth.
text.gapText: Architecture Principles. The defender's commitment ran on a policy clock rather than a treaty, and it ended when the policy did.
text.fix: Match any commitment to people in harm's way with a horizon and an exit plan decided before they fight.
